You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

jp2a
====

jp2a is a simple JPEG to ASCII converter.

The source is available at <https://github.com/cslarsen/jp2a>. This project
used to be hosted on SourceForge.

License
-------

Copyright 2006-2016 Christian Stigen Larsen  
Distributed under the GNU General Public License v2.

You can read the full license in the file COPYING. jp2a also uses other
libraries. These licenses can be found in the file LICENSES.

Usage
-----

jp2a converts JPEG images to ASCII characters. You can specify a mixture of 
files and URLs.

**Basic usage:**

```
jp2a [options] [filename(s) | URL(s)]
```

**Common options:**

- `-` - Read JPEG image from standard input
- `--size=WIDTHxHEIGHT` - Set output dimensions
- `--width=N` - Set output width (height calculated automatically)
- `--height=N` - Set output height (width calculated automatically)
- `--chars=...` - Use specific characters for output (default: "   ...',;:clodxkO0KXNWM")
- `--invert` or `-i` - Invert output image
- `--background=light` or `--background=dark` - Set background type
- `--border` or `-b` - Frame output in a border
- `--colors` - Use ANSI color for text output and CSS color for HTML output
- `--html` - Output in XHTML 1.0 format
- `--output=FILE` - Write output to file
- `--term-fit` or `-f` - Fit image to terminal display
- `--flipx` or `-x` - Flip output horizontally
- `--flipy` or `-y` - Flip output vertically
- `--help` or `-h` - Display help
- `--version` or `-V` - Print version

Examples
--------

Convert and print a JPEG file:

```
jp2a imagefile.jpg
```

Convert with specific dimensions:

```
jp2a --size=40x20 imagefile.jpg
```

Download an image from the web and convert:

```
jp2a http://example.com/image.jpg
```

Use specific characters for output:

```
jp2a --chars=" ...ooxx@@" picture.jpg
```

Read from standard input:

```
cat image.jpg | jp2a --width=76 -
```

Use with ImageMagick to convert other image formats:

```
convert somefile.png jpg:- | jp2a - --width=80
```

Output to HTML:

```
jp2a --html --output=output.html image.jpg
```

For more detailed information, see the man page: `man jp2a`

.TP

Use the given characters when producing the output ASCII image.  Default is "   ...',;:clodxkO0KXNWM".
.TP
.BI \-\-colors
Use ANSI color for text output and CSS color for HTML output.
.TP

Print debugging information when using libcurl to download images from the net.
.TP
.B \-f \-\-term\-fit
Use the largest dimension that makes the image fit in your terminal display.
.TP
.B \-\-term\-height
Use terminal display height and calculate width based on image aspect ratio.
.TP
.B \-\-term\-width
Use terminal display width and calculate height based on image aspect ratio.
.TP
.B \-z \-\-term\-zoom
Use terminal display width and height.
.TP
.B \-\-fill
When used with \-\-html and \-\-color, then color each output character's background color.  For instance,
if you want to use fill-output on a light background, do

To do the same on a light background:

jp2a --color --html --html-fill --background=dark somefile.jpg --output=light.html

The default is to have fill disabled.
.TP
.B \-x \-\-flipx
Flip output image horizontally
.TP
.B \-y \-\-flipy
Flip output image vertically
.TP
.BI \-\-height= N
Set output height.  If only --height is specified, then output width will
be calculated according to the source images aspect ratio.
.TP
.B \-h \-\-help

.TP

Converts image to grayscale when using \-\-html or \-\-colors.

.TP

.TP

.TP

a display with light characters on a dark background, you shoudl invert the image.

.BI \-\-red= ...

.BI \-\-green= ...
.TP

.PP
.B curl
\-s

.B convert
\- jpg:- |

\-
.SH DOWNLOADING IMAGES FROM THE NET
If you have compiled jp2a with libcurl(3), you can download images by specifying URLs:

.B jp2a
https://user:pass@foo.com/bar.jpg

The protocols recognized are ftp, ftps, file, http, https and tftp.

If you need more control of the downloading, you should use curl(1) or wget(1) and jp2a
read the image from standard input.

jp2a uses pipe and fork to download images using libcurl (i.e., no exec or system calls) 
and therefore does not worry about malevolently formatted URLs.
.SH GRAYSCALE CONVERSION
You can extract the red channel by doing this:

.B jp2a
somefile.jpg --red=1.0 --green=0.0 --blue=0.0

This will calculate luminance based on Y = R*1.0 + G*0.0 + B*0.0.  The default
values is to use Y = R*0.2989 + G*0.5866 + B*0.1145.

jp2a does not interpolate when resizing.  If you want better quality, try using convert(1)
and convert the source image to the exact output dimensions before using jp2a.

precise output image, and will probably be corrected in future versions.

import subprocess, os, tempfile
from PIL import Image
import io

def run_jp2a(args, stdin_data=None):
    env={"TERM":"xterm","COLUMNS":"80","LINES":"24","PATH":os.environ.get("PATH","")}
    if isinstance(args, str):
        args=[args]
    result=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True)
    # Don't pass env to keep default TERM handling? But for width tests we don't need term.
    # Actually run without TERM for explicit width tests to avoid TERM error
    return result

# Actually run without env modification for width tests
def run_simple(args, stdin=None):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=stdin, capture_output=True)
    return r.stdout.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), r.stderr.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), r.returncode

# Test 1: create 3x1 image with values 0,127,255
def make_jpeg(pixels, width, height):
    # pixels is list of (r,g,b) tuples
    im=Image.new("RGB", (width, height))
    im.putdata(pixels)
    buf=io.BytesIO()
    im.save(buf, format="JPEG", quality=100, subsampling=0)
    return buf.getvalue()

# 3x1 : black, gray 127, white
pixels=[(0,0,0),(127,127,127),(255,255,255)]
data=make_jpeg(pixels,3,1)
open("/tmp/test3x1.jpg","wb").write(data)
for chars in ["AB","01"," .#","ABCDEFGHIJ"]:
    out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=3","--height=1",f"--chars={chars}","/tmp/test3x1.jpg"])
    print(f"chars {chars!r} => out {out!r} rc{rc} err{err[:100]}")

# Try with invert
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=3","--height=1","--chars=AB","--invert","/tmp/test3x1.jpg"])
print("invert AB",repr(out))

# Try 2x1 black white
pixels2=[(0,0,0),(255,255,255)]
data2=make_jpeg(pixels2,2,1)
open("/tmp/test2x1.jpg","wb").write(data2)
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=2","--height=1","--chars=AB","/tmp/test2x1.jpg"])
print("2x1 AB",repr(out))
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=2","--height=1","--chars=AB","--invert","/tmp/test2x1.jpg"])
print("2x1 AB invert",repr(out))

# Try 1x2 vertical?
pixels3=[(0,0,0),(255,255,255)] # need 1x2
data3=make_jpeg([(0,0,0),(255,255,255)],1,2)
# actually putdata for 1x2: two pixels vertical
im=Image.new("RGB",(1,2))
im.putdata([(0,0,0),(255,255,255)])
buf=io.BytesIO()
im.save(buf,format="JPEG",quality=100,subsampling=0)
open("/tmp/test1x2.jpg","wb").write(buf.getvalue())
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=1","--height=2","--chars=AB","/tmp/test1x2.jpg"])
print("1x2 AB",repr(out))

# Test flip
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=2","--height=1","--chars=AB","--flipx","/tmp/test2x1.jpg"])
print("flipx",repr(out))
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=1","--height=2","--chars=AB","--flipy","/tmp/test1x2.jpg"])
print("flipy",repr(out))

# Test border with this
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=2","--height=1","--chars=AB","--border","/tmp/test2x1.jpg"])
print("border 2x1",repr(out))

# Test grayscale weights
# red 1.0
out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=3","--height=1","--chars=AB","--red=1.0","--green=0","--blue=0","/tmp/test3x1.jpg"])
print("red 1.0",repr(out))
# Create color test: red, green, blue pixels
im=Image.new("RGB",(3,1))
im.putdata([(255,0,0),(0,255,0),(0,0,255)])
buf=io.BytesIO()
im.save(buf,format="JPEG",quality=100,subsampling=0)
open("/tmp/rgb.jpg","wb").write(buf.getvalue())
for w in [0.2989,0.5,1.0]:
    out,err,rc=run_simple(["--width=3","--height=1","--chars=ABCDEFGHIJ",f"--red={w}",f"--green={0.587 if w!=1 else 0}",f"--blue={1-w-0.587 if w!=1 else 0}","/tmp/rgb.jpg"])
    print(f"rgb weights {w} out {repr(out)}")

func lum(r,g,b uint8) uint8 { return uint8(0.2989*float64(r)+0.5866*float64(g)+0.1145*float64(b)+0.5) }

func main(){
    path:="assets/logo-40x25-gray.jpg"
    f,_:=os.Open(path)
    img,_:=jpeg.Decode(f)

    srcW:=40; srcH:=25
    cmd:=exec.Command("./executable","--width=10",path)
    out,_:=cmd.Output()
    lines:=bytes.Split(out, []byte("\n"))
    chars:=`   ...',;:clodxkO0KXNWM`
    n:=len(chars)
    for outY:=0;outY<3;outY++{
        target:=string(lines[outY])

                    l:=lum(uint8(r>>8),uint8(g>>8),uint8(bb>>8))
                    idx:=(int(l)*(n-1)+127)/255
                    if chars[idx]==tar{
                        idealX:=outX*srcW/10
                        idealY:=outY*srcH/3
                        dist:= (sx-idealX)*(sx-idealX)+(sy-idealY)*(sy-idealY)
                        if dist<bestDist{
                            bestDist=dist
                            bestSX=sx

{"command":"cat > /workspace/main.go.orig <<'GO'
orig
GO
# We need to make a decision: Our Go reimplementation will not be pixel-perfect for downsampling, but we can try to get close by using Go's image/jpeg and point sampling.

func printHelp() { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, helpStr) }

func getTerminalSize() (int,int){
    colsStr:=os.Getenv("COLUMNS")
    linesStr:=os.Getenv("LINES")
    cols,err1:=strconv.Atoi(colsStr)
    lines,err2:=strconv.Atoi(linesStr)
    if err1!=nil || cols<=0{ cols=80}
    if err2!=nil || lines<=0{ lines=24}
    return cols, lines
}

func parseArgs(args []string) (Config, []string, error){
    cfg:=Config{
        chars:"   ...',;:clodxkO0KXNWM",
        red:0.2989, green:0.5866, blue:0.1145,
        htmlFontSize:4, htmlTitle:"jp2a converted image",
    }
    var files []string
    for _,arg:=range args{
        if arg=="-"{files=append(files,arg); continue}
        if arg=="-b"||arg=="--border"{cfg.border=true; continue}
        if arg=="-i"||arg=="--invert"{cfg.invert=!cfg.invert; continue}
        if arg=="-x"||arg=="--flipx"{cfg.flipx=true; continue}
        if arg=="-y"||arg=="--flipy"{cfg.flipy=true; continue}
        if arg=="-f"||arg=="--term-fit"{cfg.termFit=true; continue}
        if arg=="-z"||arg=="--term-zoom"{cfg.termZoom=true; continue}
        if arg=="-v"||arg=="--verbose"{cfg.verbose=true; continue}
        if arg=="-d"||arg=="--debug"{cfg.debug=true; continue}
        if arg=="-h"||arg=="--help"{printHelp(); os.Exit(0)}
        if arg=="-V"||arg=="--version"{printVersion(); os.Exit(0)}
        if strings.HasPrefix(arg,"--background="){
            val:=strings.TrimPrefix(arg,"--background=")
            if val=="dark"{cfg.invert=false}else if val=="light"{cfg.invert=true}else{return cfg,nil,fmt.Errorf("Unknown option %s",arg)}
            continue
        }
        if strings.HasPrefix(arg,"--chars="){cfg.chars=strings.TrimPrefix(arg,"--chars="); cfg.charsSet=true; continue}
        if arg=="--colors"{cfg.colors=true; continue}

package main

import (

func check(env map[string]string, args []string){

    cmd.Env=envList
    var out bytes.Buffer
    var errBuf bytes.Buffer
    cmd.Stdout=&out
    cmd.Stderr=&errBuf
    cmd.Run()
    s:=errBuf.String()
    if len(s)>200{ s=s[:200] }

}
